originality.rationale: Compared exact objective, graph, feasible cone and values, not merely titles. The 2004 FMMC paper states general SDP and treats no closed-form balanced double stars; the 2007 symmetry paper treats two *cliques* joined by a bridge (an ambient supergraph) with positive optimal internal clique edges, not the zero-internal-edge-constrained optimum on a tree. Its spectral block formula at zero internal weight is relevant but does not by itself give the globally minimized constrained solution nor uniqueness without orbit restrictions. The 2006 path theorem covers k=1 only; the continuous-time rate-budget and common-center fused stars are different. value.rationale: This gives a globally unique exact stochastic transition design for a natural diameter-three tree family, not merely a symmetric subproblem. The graph-wide Rayleigh certificate is sharp and forces all individual edge weights. The optimal gap decays as 1/k rather than the 1/k^2 of standard maximum-degree or Metropolis weights, an unbounded relative advantage with mathematical significance for bridge-mediated mixing. The k=1 boundary is known and explicitly separated from k>=2.
